chapter: Back to Los Angeles and joining Basie
title: Arranging in China and the best arrangement, 'Alice Blue Gown'
summary: He wrote constantly for his band; the 'Alice Blue Gown' swing arrangement was considered the best.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Well I was, funnily enough, I was going to say to you, during the time now you were in China and everything, you'd been arranging more and more?
Oh yes, yes. Every day I'd stay up, I'd stay up sometimes all night writing music. Sleep in the day and go to work and stay
No, no. Well would you be writing originals or would you be writing arrangements on pop tunes and things?
One of the best arrangements we had was 'Alice Blue Gown'.
But I was also writing all kinds of jazz and Duke Ellington numbers. But for some reason 'Alice Blue Gown' I believe was what everybody considered to be our best arrangement.
What sort of tempo did you take that at?
Medium swing tempo. And that was a good arrangement.
That has not been, usually that was played as a sort of slow ballad or something.
Yes, but we swung it. It was a good arrangement.
You ought to point that out to Basie.
